dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For each natural number n, this is the type of n-by-n matrices with real entries, represented as functions Fin n -> Fin n -> Real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes both A and dB arbitrary square real matrices of the same dimension n.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For an n-by-n real matrix M, this is sqrt(sum_i sum_j (M i j)^2), with both indices ranging over every element of Fin n; it is the Frobenius norm of M.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies all three norms in the inequality: the norm of the matrix product on the left and the norms of A and dB on the right.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: For n-by-n matrices A and B, this is their matrix product using the finite real dot-product multiplication instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the matrix inside the left-hand Frobenius norm equal to the ordinary matrix product A dB, not an entrywise product.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the binary multiplication operation from an HMul instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: At the explicit target occurrence, the selected HMul instance is induced by real multiplication, so the two Frobenius norms on the right are multiplied as real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the less-than-or-equal relation from an LE instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms the non-strict inequality between the real-valued norm on the left and the real-valued product on the right.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the type of natural numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The universally quantified natural number n determines the common matrix dimension and may be zero.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Matrix entries, finite sums, square roots, norms, multiplication, and both sides of the inequality are real-valued.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: This equips the real numbers with their standard less-than-or-equal relation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the target comparison the usual real inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This equips the real numbers with their standard multiplication.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines the scalar product of the two norms on the right and the multiplication of real entries used in matrix dot products.

dependency_coverage.name: instHMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Given an ordinary multiplication operation on a type, this constructs homogeneous multiplication HMul on that same type using the ordinary operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Applied to Real, it ensures that HMul.hMul on the right-hand side is ordinary real multiplication.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.meaning: For n, Fin n is the canonical finite index type with n elements, corresponding to indices 0 through n-1.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It provides the row, column, and contracted indices of the n-by-n matrices.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin.fintype
dependency_coverage.meaning: This provides the finite enumeration of all elements of Fin n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It permits all matrix indices, including the contracted matrix-product index, to be summed over finitely.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.sum
dependency_coverage.meaning: This sums the values of a function over a finite set using the supplied additive commutative monoid.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It constructs the sums of squared entries in each Frobenius norm and the finite sums occurring in matrix multiplication.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.univ
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a finite type, this is the finite set containing every element of that type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes each norm sum range over every row and every column index in Fin n.

dependency_coverage.name: HPow.hPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the exponentiation operation from an HPow instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the selected real-by-natural power instance and exponent 2, it squares each real matrix entry.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix
dependency_coverage.meaning: A matrix with row type m, column type n, and entries in alpha is represented as a function m -> n -> alpha.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the pointwise representation of A, dB, and their product and establishes that their entries are addressed by two Fin n indices.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix.instHMulOfFintypeOfMulOfAddCommMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: For compatible matrices M and N over a finitely indexed additive and multiplicative type, this defines their product by (M N) i k = sum_j M i j * N j k.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expands LocalDef003 n A dB into ordinary matrix multiplication, so its (i,k) entry is sum_j A i j * dB j k.

dependency_coverage.name: Monoid.toNatPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: This equips a monoid with exponentiation by natural numbers using repeated monoid multiplication.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For the multiplicative monoid of real numbers, exponent 2 evaluates each entry's power as its real square.

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This interprets a natural-number literal in a type that has the corresponding OfNat instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets the literal 2 used as the natural exponent in the norm definition.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddCommMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: This equips the real numbers with their standard addition and additive identity as an additive commutative monoid.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the addition and zero used by finite sums in the Frobenius norms and matrix dot products.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: This equips the real numbers with their standard multiplication and multiplicative identity as a monoid.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies natural-number exponentiation of real entries, in particular their squares.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.sqrt
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the nonnegative real square-root operation, implemented through the square root of the nonnegative part of its input.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It takes the square root of each sum of entrywise squares. These inputs are nonnegative, so it is the ordinary nonnegative square root.

dependency_coverage.name: instHPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: Given a power operation Pow alpha beta, this constructs the corresponding homogeneous-result HPow alpha beta alpha instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It exposes real exponentiation by natural numbers through HPow.hPow in the Frobenius-norm definition.

dependency_coverage.name: instOfNatNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This interprets each natural-number literal n as that same value in Nat.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the exponent literal 2 exactly the natural number two.

binders: n is an arbitrary natural number; it is an implicit universally quantified binder in Lean.
A and dB are arbitrary n-by-n matrices with real entries, equivalently functions Fin n -> Fin n -> Real.
conclusions: sqrt(sum_i sum_k (sum_j A_ij * dB_jk)^2) <= sqrt(sum_i sum_j A_ij^2) * sqrt(sum_i sum_j dB_ij^2), where every index ranges over Fin n.
mathematical_definitions: For an n-by-n real matrix M, define its Frobenius norm by ||M||_F = sqrt(sum_{i=0}^{n-1} sum_{j=0}^{n-1} M_ij^2).
Define the matrix product by (A dB)_ik = sum_{j=0}^{n-1} A_ij * dB_jk.
Empty finite sums are zero, so these definitions also apply when n = 0.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every natural number n and every pair of n-by-n real matrices A and dB, the Frobenius norm of their ordinary matrix product is at most the product of their Frobenius norms: ||A dB||_F <= ||A||_F ||dB||_F.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: Only finite square matrices over the real numbers are covered; rectangular matrices and other scalar fields are not quantified.
There are no assumptions on A or dB: neither invertibility, positivity, normalization, nor nonzeroness is required.
The identifier dB carries no encoded perturbation meaning; dB is an arbitrary matrix with no smallness or relationship-to-another-matrix condition.
The multiplicative bound has exact constant 1.
The case n = 0 is included. It is degenerate rather than logically vacuous: the unique empty matrices have zero Frobenius norm, and the conclusion reduces to 0 <= 0.
The proposition concerns exact real arithmetic and encodes no floating-point operations, rounding errors, probabilistic statements, or computed approximations.
The norm is specifically the entrywise Frobenius norm, not an operator or spectral norm.
No equality characterization, strict inequality, or optimality assertion beyond the displayed bound is encoded.
